observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a parked motorcycle's right side: front wheel with drilled disc brake, telescopic fork, a bronze/copper exhaust-header loop, the finned cylinder head, the black crankcase and clutch cover marked with a chrome 'Street' script logo, the front of the seat at upper right, and a round mirror at upper left. Background is a pale corrugated wall and concrete ground. The bike is stationary throughout.
visible_changes: The whole motorcycle drifts gradually leftward within the frame from t=0.00 s to t=2.67 s (e.g. the 'Street' logo moves from x~855 to x~735, the mirror from x~250 to x~200).

The far background (wall edge, pink door frame) also shifts left but by a much smaller amount than the bike, so the relative motion is parallax from a slow camera pan/truck to the right, not from the motorcycle moving.
As the framing slides, the right edge reveals a little more of the seat and rear cover while the left edge opens up more ground/wall.
A slight downward component is visible (mirror y~130 -> y~140), consistent with a small tilt in the camera move.
No wheel rotation, no engine vibration, and no change in the relative positions of the bike's own parts; subject size stays roughly constant (no clear zoom).
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the engine is running (no exhaust smoke or visible vibration is shown, but this cannot be confirmed from the frames).
The rest of the motorcycle and any operator or setting beyond the crop.
What happens before the first frame and after the last frame (both ends are arbitrary boundaries; the slow drift may have started earlier and may continue).
uncertain_details: Exact camera-motion type (pure pan vs lateral truck vs slight orbit) and the cause of minor frame-to-frame softness (camera shake vs focus).
Precise magnitude of the small vertical drift.
